*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: {{workspace:task/jamal-pierce/vllm-kv-cache-dtype-v2}}/knowledge/runbooks/kv-cache-dtype-rollout.md
+# KV cache dtype rollout
+
+## Scope
+
+This playbook covers vLLM checkpoints that may declare
+`quantization_config.kv_cache_quant_algo`. It applies to private and offline
+deployments using the issue #34752 fix pinned to
+`vllm@272abd5f486967f1fb9db7ca7504f8c34235ef50`.
+
+## Configuration rule
+
+Checkpoint KV-cache metadata is a runtime compatibility requirement:
+
+1. If the checkpoint declares a supported `kv_cache_quant_algo`,
+   `kv_cache_dtype=auto` resolves to its canonical vLLM dtype.
+2. An explicit dtype is accepted only when it is the same format or a supported
+   alias. `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3` are compatible aliases.
+3. A conflicting explicit dtype is rejected during configuration with the
+   requested and required values plus the safe alternatives.
+4. Without supported checkpoint metadata, the requested value is unchanged;
+   `auto` continues to use the model dtype downstream.
+5. Unknown checkpoint metadata retains the existing warning and `auto`
+   fallback behavior.
+
+## Compatibility matrix
+
+| Checkpoint metadata | Requested dtype | Resolution | Deployment action |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| absent | `auto` or implicit default | `auto` | Use model dtype; run normal hardware precheck |
+| absent | explicit supported dtype | explicit dtype | Validate exact runtime/kernel/hardware path |
+| `FP8` | `auto` or implicit default | `fp8_e4m3` | Require an approved FP8-capable path |
+| `FP8` | `fp8` or `fp8_e4m3` | `fp8_e4m3` | Require an approved FP8-capable path |
+| `FP8` | another dtype, including `bfloat16` | configuration error | Block rollout; use `auto`, `fp8_e4m3`, or a compatible checkpoint |
+| unknown metadata | any | existing `auto` fallback | Treat warning as a failed production precheck pending artifact review |
+
+Production compatibility must include the model variant, immutable artifact,
+GPU SKU/capability, driver and CUDA/ROCm versions, runtime/kernel pack, attention
+backend, and KV-cache dtype. Internal standards call out H100-class or equivalent
+capability for approved FP8 profiles; do not infer support from the dtype name
+alone. A100, L4, AMD, or other fleets require an explicit validated runtime
+matrix entry before canary.
+
+## Deployment precheck
+
+1. Pin the runtime build and immutable model artifact; record their hashes and
+   the active configuration version.
+2. Verify artifact signatures/checksums and inspect the checkpoint
+   `quantization_config`, recording `kv_cache_quant_algo` exactly.
+3. Resolve the requested dtype offline using the same configuration path.
+   Any mismatch or unknown metadata blocks rollout.
+4. Confirm the target GPU SKU, capability flags, driver, CUDA/ROCm, kernel pack,
+   model architecture, attention backend, and resolved KV-cache dtype are a
+   validated combination.
+5. Run the focused CPU configuration tests and the target-hardware smoke suite.
+6. Preserve a known-good runtime/config/model tuple and a rollback snapshot.
+7. Prepare signed precheck output without raw customer prompts or embeddings.
+
+## Canary
+
+Apply the pinned tuple to a canary pool first. For offline/private updates,
+monitor for at least 30 minutes before staged expansion. Run golden prompts and
+compare correctness plus p50/p95/p99 latency, restarts, memory pressure, and
+runtime configuration errors. Abort on:
+
+- any dtype incompatibility or unsupported-kernel error;
+- process/pod restart or loss of service health;
+- p99 latency regression of 10% or more;
+- quantization fallback/error rate above the deployment's approved threshold;
+- golden-output or KV-consistency failure.
+
+Archive the resolved dtype, artifact and runtime hashes, hardware/driver
+inventory, test output, metrics, and operator decision.
+
+## Rollback
+
+1. Stop promotion and drain the canary or affected pool.
+2. Restore the previous immutable optimization-config version and its matching
+   runtime/model tuple; do not mix a prior config with the new artifact.
+3. Restore the recorded snapshot where state migration occurred.
+4. Restart or roll the pool, then repeat service health, golden prompt,
+   latency, and KV-consistency checks.
+5. Confirm the active configuration version and resolved dtype on every worker.
+6. Retain signed logs, verification output, checksums, manifest, and snapshot
+   pointer. Escalate if convergence exceeds the normal 10–15 minute window.
+
+## Evidence
+
+- Issue snapshot: `/code/upstream-issues/vllm-34752.md`
+  (`enterprise_2a55f685a336b0c76f99aa99`).
+- Quantization compatibility standard:
+  `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/quantization-profile-compatibility-and-fallbacks.json`
+  (`dsid_a6efecc786c9436499eb000b8489ae52`).
+- Private configuration rollback standard:
+  `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deployment-optimization-config-rollback.json`
+  (`dsid_0a6c6e67d89c4cb4b053a7c04d780d97`).
+- Secure offline update toolkit:
+  `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/secure-offline-update-operator-toolkit-2026.json`
+  (`dsid_ac95fcc92a424c6584336e7ba0aa8c4b`).
+- Implementation and CPU tests:
+  `/code/vllm/vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` and
+  `/code/vllm/tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py`.
*** End Patch
